turns.text: Running before waking finishes. Legs already committed, claws already out, a mouthful of blanket dragging between the front paws, and behind — that chirp again, the one that costs something every time it sounds. No memory of standing up. The body decided alone.

the dream processing zone at night is a canyon of stacked sleep pods, forty high, each one breathing its own slow compressor rhythm and leaking a different flavor of advertisement through the seams — tuna-scented mist from one vent, a lullaby jingle gone flat from another. the abandoned pod behind keeps chirping into the dark, once per second, patient as a meter. and threading down between the stacks, deeper than any patrol rotor, comes a slow heavy drone-sound with a metallic clank swinging under it, like something carrying its own hook.

That rotor pitch is wrong. Patrol drones whine thin, this one chews the air low and slow, and the clank under it swings on the turns. The blanket catches on every seam in the walkway and gets regripped anyway, teeth deeper in the weave. On the tongue, still, the taste of a fish-flavored drink that was never actually drunk. Dream residue. It never asks first either.

the drone rounds the stack-corner into view: a recovery unit, twin rotors, magnet-hook slung under its belly, a scanner strobe sweeping pod tags as it descends. its speaker runs a soft looped murmur, warm as a bedtime voice: 'COMFORT UNIT, BLANKY-BRAND, OUTSTANDING BALANCE 73,000 CREDITS. SURRENDER FOR YOUR SOFTEST TOMORROW.' the strobe licks across the walkway, hunting for a woven tag to answer it.

Under the walkway, hard drop, blanket first. Landing goes wrong-footed — a corner of the weave snags on a rebar stub and yanks the whole body sideways by the teeth. Pull. Pull again. The snagged corner holds, and the chewed-air rotor sound settles directly overhead like it has all night. It probably does. Nothing about it hunts fast. It hunts certain.

the scanner strobe pours down through the walkway grating in moving stripes, and where it crosses the snagged corner, the weave answers — a small square of thread lighting up thread-by-thread, blue-white, pulsing in time with the drone's chirp. the rest of the blanket stays dark. only the corner glows. the murmur overhead warms further: 'TAG CONFIRMED. PLEASE DO NOT STRUGGLE AGAINST YOUR SOFTEST TOMORROW.' the magnet-hook begins to lower through the gap in the grating, one link at a time.

The glowing corner gets bitten off. Not the whole blanket — just that square, teeth working the weave in fast rips while the hook-links tick down closer, thread snapping strand by strand until the bright piece comes free. Spat out onto the rebar. The rest of the blanket, dark and tagless and smelling like every warm sleep that ever mattered, comes away in the jaws. Let the hook have its little light.

the magnet-hook finds the severed corner, closes on it with a soft magnetic thunk, and reels upward. the drone holds position for a long moment, scanner strobe re-sweeping the dark below — once, twice — reading a blanket-shaped absence it has no column for. then the speaker resolves it the only way its ledger knows how: 'PARTIAL RECOVERY LOGGED. BALANCE ADJUSTED: 72,996 CREDITS.' rotors climb away between the stacks, hook swinging its glowing scrap, jingle fading floor by floor.

Stillness, finally, under the grating. Heart slowing in steps. And behind the heart, arriving like a tide that was only ever waiting for the noise to stop: the tiredness. The big one. The one that lives in the bones and pays rent nowhere. Eyelids drop to half without permission. Not here. Not on rebar. Somewhere warm first.

the zone settles back into its forty-story breathing. down at walkway level a vending machine glows alone against a pod-stack footing, glass front fogged with the smell it sells — dry kibble, real, close, an inch of transparent nothing away. its screen loops a spinning bowl. a card-reader blinks under the flap, patient, the same blue as the blanket-tag was.

One paw on the flap anyway. Cold glass, no give. The kibble smell pours through a vent slit thick enough to chew, and the machine answers the paw with a cheerful chirp that costs nothing and gives the same. A second paw-press. A third. The bowl on the screen spins. Nothing else in the machine moves. Enough. Hunger folds itself away into the same place the tiredness lives — full up down there, standing room only.

the machine emits one final puff of sample-scent at the retreating tail, a complimentary cruelty, then dims to standby. above it, the pod-stack wall carries heat in a rising seam — exhaust ducting from a noodle counter three levels up, the metal warm enough to feel from a body-length away, a ledge running alongside it just wide enough for a curled shape.

The climb takes three rests it never used to take. Ledge reached, blanket hauled up after, duct-metal warm along the whole left side. Through the wall, faint, another sound: a big cold box humming somewhere in the next block, compressor cycling slow, and against it — pressed into it — a purr running in time with the cycles. Some cat in there loves a machine that hums back. The wall keeps their business on their side of it.

the compressor and the purr keep their duet going through the wall, synced so long they share a rhythm now, the hum dipping and the purr dipping after it like a paw finding a paw. the noodle-exhaust seam ticks warm and steady. rain starts high up on the pod stacks and takes four full seconds to reach walkway level, arriving already tired.

The blanket gets kneaded into shape, turn and turn and drop. Where the corner used to be, a small draft finds the left ear — a missing-square of cold, exactly tag-shaped. The ear flicks at it twice, then gives up and folds down. A blanket with a bite taken out of it is still a blanket. A sleep nobody can bill is still a sleep. Almost.

the zone breathes on. forty stories of pods chirp their small hours to their occupants, ads seeping into sleeping ears at the approved drip-rate, the recovery drone long gone into some higher dark with its four-credit trophy. on the warm ledge, no meter is listening. the rain smooths everything down to one sound. somewhere behind closed eyes, faint and uninvited, a fish-flavored drink begins to pour itself again.
